title: Kepler-10 b
why: Kepler's first confirmed rocky planet, on a 20-hour orbit. In the training set.

title: Kepler-10 c
why: Same star, much wider orbit. Never trained on, though its star's light curve was.

title: Kepler-511 c
why: A test-set planet the models call correctly and confidently.

title: Eclipsing binary
why: Classic V-shaped eclipse, and its depth changes with Kepler's seasons.

title: Glowing companion
why: Test-set false positive with a clear dip half an orbit later: the companion is a star.

title: Confident mistake
why: Test-set false positive that every model calls a planet; nothing in the brightness data gives it away.

title: Missed planet
why: A real planet (Kepler-1065 c) that both models reject; its half-orbit window shows a dip.

title: Models disagree
why: The trees say planet, the CNN says false positive. The CNN is right.

title: Very long transit
why: A 24-hour transit, longer than anything in training, so the verdict comes with a warning.

title: Undecided candidate
why: NASA hasn't ruled on this one yet; there's no right answer to check against.
